name: Clean
pattern: Explosive pull from the floor or hang: the legs and hips drive the bar up fast, then you drop under it and catch it on the front of your shoulders.
setup: Feet hip width, bar over the middle of your feet.
Hands just outside your legs, arms straight, hook grip if you know it.
Hips a bit above your knees, chest up, back flat, shoulders just over the bar.

steps.text: Brace and push the floor away; the bar leaves the floor slowly and stays close.
As the bar passes your knees, keep your back angle and shoulders over the bar.
Let the bar slide to your upper thigh as your knees move back under it.
Jump: drive hips, knees and ankles straight and shrug hard, arms still long.
Pull yourself under, whip your elbows forward and catch the bar on your shoulders in a quarter squat.
Stand tall with elbows high, then lower the bar to your thighs and the floor.

cues.cue: Long arms until your hips are straight.
cues.why: Power comes from the hips and knees; bending the arms early cuts bar speed.

cues.cue: Keep the bar close, brushing your thighs.
cues.why: A bar that swings out makes the catch harder and costs force.

cues.cue: Push the floor away; hips and shoulders rise together.
cues.why: Hips shooting up first turns the pull into a back lift and puts the bar in front of you.

cues.cue: Fast elbows: point them forward in the catch.
cues.why: High elbows make a shelf on the shoulders so the wrists do not take the load.

cues.cue: Catch soft, knees bent, heels down.
cues.why: The power clean catch absorbs energy with knee bend much like a jump landing.

cues.cue: Back flat from floor to catch.
cues.why: Rounding under load raises spinal stress and leaks force.

breathing: Big breath and brace before the pull, hold it through the catch, breathe out once you stand.

tempo.note: The pull and catch take under a second; lower under control and reset each rep.

mistakes.name: Arms pull early
mistakes.looks: Elbows bend before the hips and knees are straight.
mistakes.fix: Think of your arms as ropes until you have jumped.
mistakes.why: It slows the bar and drags it forward.

mistakes.name: Hips shoot up
mistakes.looks: Knees straighten off the floor while the chest stays down.
mistakes.fix: Chest and hips rise together; push with the legs.
mistakes.why: The back does the lift and the bar drifts away from you.

mistakes.name: Elbows drop in the catch
mistakes.looks: The bar lands in the hands with elbows pointing down.
mistakes.fix: Whip the elbows forward fast, fingers loose.
mistakes.why: The wrists and elbows take the bar instead of the shoulders.

mistakes.name: Back rounds
mistakes.looks: The lower back curves as the bar leaves the floor.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load, chest up, brace before you pull.
mistakes.why: It raises the load on the spine.

safety: Learn it with a coach and light weight; start from the hang before the floor.
Wrist or elbow pain in the catch: work on front rack mobility, use fingertips.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back; use bumper plates.

variants.change: Start standing; slide the bar to above the knee (or below for 'below the knees'), then extend. Mid-thigh starts make the highest power output.
Bar starts on blocks at the knee or thigh, no lowering phase.
Catch in a full front squat, then stand.
No drop under: arms pull the bar around to the shoulders, legs straight.
Dumbbells at your sides or one hand; same hip drive, catch on the shoulders.
The bell swings between the legs, then the arm zips up close and the bell rolls onto the forearm in the rack.
Clean first, then press, jerk or thruster from the rack; see jerk-push-press.

subtypes.name: Kettlebell clean
subtypes.change: One or two bells: hike between the legs, hinge snap, arm stays close and the bell rolls onto the forearm, wrist straight.

subtypes.name: Dumbbell clean
subtypes.change: Dumbbells hang at your sides; same hinge and jump, catch the heads on your shoulders, elbows forward.

subtypes.name: Muscle clean
subtypes.change: Legs stay straight after the extension; arms turn the bar over onto the shoulders.

subtypes.name: Hang clean
subtypes.change: Starts standing, bar slides to just above the knee, then the same extension and catch.

subtypes.name: Squat clean
subtypes.change: Catch in a deep front squat (split stance for split clean), then stand.

metrics.label: Back angle as the bar passes the knee
Knee bend in a power catch

motion.basis: Phase order (first pull, transition with knee re-bend, second pull, catch) from gourgoulis2000 and kipp2011; power-catch knee bend similar to jump landing per moolyk2013. All joint angles are estimates from typical lifter photos and coaching texts, not measured values.
